notes:
Circle

  • Standard form, centre origin: $x^2+y^2=r^2$. Centre $(h,k)$: $(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2$.
  • General form: $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ has centre $(-g,-f)$ and radius $\sqrt{g^2+f^2-c}$.

Parabola

EquationFocusDirectrixOpens
$y^2=4ax$$(a,0)$$x=-a$right
$y^2=-4ax$$(-a,0)$$x=a$left
$x^2=4ay$$(0,a)$$y=-a$up
$x^2=-4ay$$(0,-a)$$y=a$down
  • Length of latus rectum $=4a$ in every case; axis of symmetry passes through vertex and focus.

Ellipse

  • $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$. If $a>b$, major axis along $x$-axis, foci $(\pm c,0)$ with $c^2=a^2-b^2$; if $b>a$, foci are $(0,\pm c)$ with $c^2=b^2-a^2$.
  • Eccentricity $e=c/a<1$ (or $c/b$ if major axis is vertical). Latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}$ (using the semi-major axis in the denominator).

Hyperbola

  • $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, foci $(\pm c,0)$, $c^2=a^2+b^2$, eccentricity $e=c/a>1$ always.
  • Length of transverse axis $=2a$; latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}$. When $a=b$ it is called a rectangular hyperbola.

Quick comparison

  • Circle: $e=0$. Ellipse: $01$.

Exam tip

KCET sets about 2-3 questions from conics, mixed across circle, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola — mostly finding centre/radius from the general circle equation, or focus/directrix/latus rectum/eccentricity from a standard equation. Always check whether the major axis of the ellipse is along $x$ or $y$ before picking $a$ and $b$.
